version to the new 3.1.1 bin directory and now it opens and displays
correctly.

Now to make sure the packages I need to use are up to date for 3.1.1 and
time I get back to work.

Bruce

messages.subject: RE: Updating Deducer to R 3+
messages.body_plain:
Bruce,

There's a problem loading dplyr and Deducer at the same time. The most important feature in dplyr is the select function, which selects variables. Deducer loads MASS, which has its own select function. Deducer won't allow you to detach MASS as long as it's loaded. Loading dplyr again after loading Deducer might work, or using dplyr::select might work also. I've just been avoiding loading the two at the same time.

Cheers,
Bob

-----Original Message-----
From: ded...@googlegroups.com [mailto:ded...@googlegroups.com] On Behalf Of Bruce Miller
Sent: Wednesday, July 16, 2014 9:18 PM
To: ded...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Updating Deducer to R 3+

Hi Ian,

When will the next iteration of Deducer be available to run beyond R
2.15 like under R 3+?
Discovered that dplyr will not run unless R is >3 as well as many other updated packages for biology.

Bruce

Hi all,

Sorry to beat this issue to death.  Apparently I have still a screwed up installation of Deducer with R 3.1.1.  OS is Win7 64 bit but using 32 bit R.

When I followed standard install of Deducer packages using R 3.1.1
I could open Deducer, but it did not open the Data Viewer.

I found that using the deducer.exe from the older legacy R version 2.15.0  opened the Data Viewer rather than a "table" window. Yes I reinstalled Deducer using the Win installer that did reinstall the 2.15 version again on a different drive in order to look at settings to regain Data Viewer function.

I will try again this morning to delete the vestiges of R 2.15 and then need to see how to set the defaults for Deducer to open the Data Viewer in 3.1.1

What flagged the issue still lingering after last re-install was that I can not access the iNEXT package using Deducer.

If I use only the new R 3.1.1 console it worked.

This is the code was used used:
#install.packages('devtools')
library(devtools)
install_github('iNEXT','JohnsonHsieh')
library(iNEXT)

The program iNEXT (iNterpolation and EXTrapolation) is written in the R <http://www.r-project.org/> language and the interactive web application is built by using Shiny <http://www.rstudio.com/shiny/>. The user provides a vector of abundances of individual species (abundance data) or incidences of individual species (incidence data). iNEXT computes the following species richness estimates and associated 95% confidence intervals:

Hsieh, T. C., K. H. Ma, and A. Chao. 2013. iNEXT online: interpolation and extrapolation (Version 1.0) [Software]. Available from http://chao.stat.nthu.edu.tw/blog/software-download/.

I think the issue is that Deducer is somehow still linked to legacy R version 2.15.0 (2012-03-30) and even though I installed 3.1.1 Deducer is not using it.

JGR::package.manager()
> library(iNEXT)
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) :

In addition: Warning message:
package 'iNEXT' was built under R version 3.1.1
Error : unable to load R code in package 'iNEXT'
Error: package/namespace load failed for 'iNEXT'

Cheers from a frustrated user

Bruce

Hi Bruce,

Sorry for the delayed response. It sounds like you may have a corrupted set-up after so many changes. Let's see if we can get you up and running.

First open R-3.1.1 and run
install.packages("JGR")
install.packages("Deducer")
library(JGR)
JGR()

make sure that the version of R that you open (32/64-bit) is the same as the version of java that you have installed.

If that doesn't bring up JGR, then let me know the output of

.libPaths()

If one of these paths is old (i.e. it is something like \Documents\win-library\2.15\, then delete all of the folders inside of that directory and try again.

Best,
Ian
